chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd: Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Hamiri both narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Exalted God sent Adam (peace be upon him) down from Paradise, He sent down with him one hundred and twenty branches: forty of which are edible both inside and outside; forty of which are edible inside but the outside is cast away; and forty of which are edible outside but the inside is cast away. And a sack containing the seed of everything.

key_terms.أَهْبَطَ: Sent down (from a higher place to earth)
key_terms.قَضِيب: Branch or stalk (of a fruit tree)

ai.seo_question: What types of fruits and provisions did God send down with Adam from Paradise?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these 120 branches to illustrate the comprehensive nature of divine sustenance provided at humanity's descent, reflecting the Shia emphasis on God's mercy in equipping Earth for human habitation. The specific classification of fruits by internal and external edibility highlights the intricate wisdom in the creation of agricultural diversity, while the 'sack of seeds' symbolizes the potential for all plant life to emerge from this primordial provision.
